Edit the 3D by hand

Drag the corners of the faceted sculpture to correct it: a muzzle, an ear, a foot. Shift while dragging moves the corner straight in or out of the surface; dropped on a corner next to it, the two become one (a face less); Alt + click on a face adds a corner there (two faces more); Ctrl + click on a corner, or Delete with the pointer on it, removes it (⌘ + click on the Mac); Shift + Alt + click near a side turns the diagonal between its two faces; dragged from its middle, a whole face moves (with Shift straight in or out). The pieces, the sheets and the quote are recalculated; the edits stay in the project and come back when the sculpture is recalculated with the same faces.

Detail brush

Each click adds an area: "more detail" keeps faces (muzzle, paws), "less detail" removes them (back, flanks). The total number of faces stays as set.

Sheet and cutting
°

0° = every face is a separate piece. Higher = larger sections to bend and fewer welds.

Base plate

Structure and stability

Flat frames across the sculpture, welded inside the shell: they keep large sculptures from flexing. Each rib is engraved with its number and distance from the end.

2D parts

Flat parts drawn to measure that go with the work (brackets, fixing plates, a plaque): same material, their own thickness (empty = that of the work), nested by thickness, with their engravings and texts in the DXF, and in the quote.
